comment: Generated by tools/dev/gen_app_map.py: edit that file. Windows app -> what to use on HalOS. kind: native | wine | web | alternative | none | not_needed. targets, best first: featured:<Store pick> repo:<Arch> flatpak:<Flathub id> aur:<AUR> winget:<Windows build for Wine> url:<official download or web app>.

apps.name: Opera GX
apps.why: Opera GX has no Linux build; regular Opera does and signs in to the same Opera account.

apps.name: Arc
apps.why: Arc has no Linux build; Zen Browser has the same sidebar-and-spaces layout.

apps.name: Microsoft Teams
apps.why: Microsoft's own Linux client was retired; Teams for Linux wraps the official web app with notifications and screen sharing.

apps.name: WhatsApp
apps.why: WhatsApp has no Linux app; WhatsApp Web is the same account. ZapZap wraps it as a desktop app.

apps.name: LINE
apps.why: LINE has no Linux app; its Chrome extension is the official way.

apps.name: Microsoft Outlook
apps.why: Outlook has no Linux app; Outlook on the web is the same mailbox, and Thunderbird can use the account too.

apps.name: iTunes
apps.alternative: Apple Music on the web, or Rhythmbox for a local library
apps.why: iTunes has no Linux build. Your music files play in any player; iPhone photos are handled by the iPhone step.

apps.name: Apple Music
apps.why: Apple Music's web player is the same library; Cider is a desktop client for it.

apps.name: iCloud
apps.why: iCloud Drive, Photos, Mail and Notes all work at icloud.com. Passwords come across through the iCloud Passwords export.

apps.name: Apple Devices
apps.why: iPhone photos and files are read with libimobiledevice, which HalOS includes.

apps.name: foobar2000
apps.why: foobar2000 runs well under Wine; Strawberry is the closest native player.

apps.name: MPC-HC
apps.why: Codecs are built in on Linux, so no codec pack is needed.

apps.name: DaVinci Resolve
apps.why: Blackmagic ships an official Linux build (needs an NVIDIA or AMD GPU).

apps.name: Streamlabs Desktop
apps.why: Streamlabs is OBS underneath; OBS Studio imports its scenes.

apps.name: Voicemod
apps.why: Voicemod needs a Windows audio driver.

apps.name: Paint.NET
apps.why: Pinta is a Paint.NET-style editor made for Linux.

apps.name: Adobe Photoshop
apps.alternative: Photopea (opens PSD in the browser) or GIMP
apps.why: Adobe's installer and licensing don't work under Wine.

apps.name: Adobe Illustrator
apps.why: Adobe's installer and licensing don't work under Wine.

apps.name: Adobe Premiere Pro
apps.why: Adobe's installer and licensing don't work under Wine.

apps.name: Adobe After Effects
apps.why: Adobe's installer and licensing don't work under Wine.

apps.name: Adobe Lightroom
apps.why: Lightroom on the web also works at lightroom.adobe.com.

apps.name: Adobe Creative Cloud
apps.why: The Creative Cloud installer doesn't work under Wine.

apps.name: Adobe Acrobat Reader
apps.why: HalOS opens, annotates and signs PDFs with Okular.

apps.name: Figma
apps.why: Figma is a web app; Figma Linux wraps it with local fonts.

apps.name: Affinity
apps.why: Affinity v2 runs under a tuned Wine build; expect some setup.

apps.name: AutoCAD
apps.alternative: FreeCAD or LibreCAD; AutoCAD Web for DWG
apps.why: AutoCAD doesn't run under Wine.

apps.name: Fusion 360
apps.why: Fusion runs under Wine with a community installer; FreeCAD is the native choice.

apps.name: Microsoft Office
apps.alternative: LibreOffice, or Office on the web with the same Microsoft account
apps.why: Microsoft 365's click-to-run installer doesn't work under Wine. Your .docx, .xlsx and .pptx files open in LibreOffice or ONLYOFFICE.

apps.name: Microsoft OneDrive
apps.why: The open-source OneDrive client syncs the same account; KDE can also browse OneDrive in Files.

apps.name: Notion
apps.why: Notion has no official Linux app; the web app is the same workspace.

apps.name: Grammarly
apps.why: Grammarly's browser extension works on Linux.

apps.name: Visual Studio
apps.alternative: VS Code with the C# Dev Kit, or JetBrains Rider
apps.why: Visual Studio is Windows-only; .NET itself is native on Linux.

apps.name: Google Antigravity
apps.why: Google publishes a Linux build of Antigravity.

apps.name: Claude
apps.why: Claude runs as a web app at claude.ai; a community desktop build is on the AUR. Your Claude settings and history are brought across by the History step.

apps.name: Ollama
apps.why: HalOS reuses the models already downloaded on Windows.

apps.name: Git
apps.why: Git is already part of HalOS.

apps.name: TortoiseGit
apps.alternative: GitHub Desktop; Files shows Git status itself

apps.name: Python
apps.why: Python is already part of HalOS.

apps.name: Notepad++
apps.why: Notepad++ also runs under Wine if you want the exact app.

apps.name: PuTTY
apps.why: ssh is built in to the terminal too.

apps.name: WinSCP
apps.alternative: FileZilla; Files also opens sftp:// addresses

apps.name: WSL
apps.why: HalOS is Linux, so WSL isn't needed.

apps.name: Unreal Engine
apps.why: Epic publishes Linux builds of Unreal Engine.

apps.name: Roblox Studio
apps.why: Vinegar runs Roblox Studio with a tuned Wine.

apps.name: MATLAB
apps.why: MathWorks ships a Linux build under the same licence.

apps.name: AutoHotkey
apps.why: AutoHotkey scripts drive Windows APIs and don't run on Linux.

apps.name: Steam
apps.why: Steam on Linux runs most Windows games through Proton, with the same library.

apps.name: Epic Games Launcher
apps.why: Heroic signs in to your Epic account and runs the games through Proton.

apps.name: GOG Galaxy
apps.why: Heroic signs in to GOG too.

apps.name: Amazon Games
apps.why: Heroic signs in to Amazon Games too.

apps.name: Battle.net
apps.why: Battle.net installs through Lutris and its games run with Wine.

apps.name: EA app
apps.why: EA's launcher runs through Lutris or as part of an EA game on Steam.

apps.name: Ubisoft Connect
apps.why: Ubisoft Connect installs through Lutris.

apps.name: Minecraft Launcher
apps.why: Minecraft Java Edition is native; Prism Launcher signs in with your Microsoft account.

apps.name: Roblox
apps.why: Sober runs Roblox on Linux.

apps.name: Valorant
apps.why: Valorant's Vanguard anti-cheat is a Windows kernel driver; it can't run on Linux. Keep Windows for it (Restart into Windows).

apps.name: League of Legends
apps.why: League of Legends needs Vanguard, a Windows kernel driver. Keep Windows for it.

apps.name: Fortnite
apps.alternative: GeForce NOW or Xbox Cloud Gaming
apps.why: Fortnite's anti-cheat refuses Linux. It can be played through Xbox Cloud Gaming or GeForce NOW in a browser.

apps.name: Xbox
apps.why: Game Pass games play in the browser through Xbox Cloud Gaming.

apps.name: CurseForge
apps.why: CurseForge has a Linux build; Minecraft packs also install through Prism Launcher.

apps.name: Wallpaper Engine
apps.why: Wallpaper Engine runs from Steam with Proton; the Settings step can also set up a free animated wallpaper.

apps.name: Vortex
apps.alternative: Lutris installs Vortex; Mod Organizer 2 also works through Proton

apps.name: 7-Zip
apps.why: Archives open in Files (Ark) already; 7zip adds the command-line tool.

apps.name: KeePass
apps.why: KeePassXC opens the same .kdbx database.

apps.name: LastPass
apps.why: LastPass works through its browser extension.

apps.name: WireGuard
apps.why: WireGuard tunnels import straight into Network settings.

apps.name: Google Drive
apps.alternative: Google Drive in Files (KDE online accounts), or rclone
apps.why: Google has no Linux Drive client; KDE shows Drive as a folder in Files.

apps.name: Microsoft PowerToys
apps.alternative: KDE has window tiling, a launcher, colour picker and key remapping built in

apps.name: CCleaner
apps.why: Linux has no registry to clean.

apps.name: Rufus
apps.alternative: KDE ISO Image Writer or Ventoy

apps.name: CrystalDiskInfo
apps.alternative: KDiskMark and KDE's disk health (SMART) page

apps.name: OpenRGB
apps.why: OpenRGB controls most motherboard, RAM and peripheral lighting.

apps.name: KDE Connect
apps.why: KDE Connect and SAINT Link pair your phone with HalOS.

apps.name: Samsung Magician
apps.alternative: KDE's disk health page; firmware updates come through fwupd

apps.name: Quick Assist
apps.alternative: RustDesk or KDE's remote desktop sharing

apps.name: Cortana
apps.why: SAINT is HalOS's assistant.

apps.name: SAINT
apps.why: SAINT is built in to HalOS; its history and settings are merged by the History step.

apps.name: Quicken
apps.why: Quicken has no Linux build and runs poorly under Wine.

apps.name: TurboTax
apps.why: TurboTax Online covers the same returns.

apps.name: QuickBooks
apps.why: QuickBooks Online is the supported route; the desktop edition doesn't run under Wine.

apps.name: FL Studio
apps.why: FL Studio has no Linux build; it runs with Wine (Image-Line does not support it there). LMMS and Bitwig are native alternatives.

apps.name: Bloxstrap
apps.why: Roblox has no official Linux build; Sober runs the Roblox player, and Vinegar runs Roblox Studio.

apps.name: BlueStacks
apps.why: BlueStacks is Windows-only; Waydroid runs Android apps on HalOS.

apps.name: ComfyUI
apps.why: ComfyUI runs natively on Linux from its repository (the desktop wrapper is Windows and macOS only).

apps.name: Inno Setup
apps.why: Inno Setup builds Windows installers; it isn't needed on HalOS (it does run with Wine if you still build them).

apps.name: ASIO4ALL
apps.why: Low-latency audio is built in to HalOS (PipeWire); ASIO drivers aren't used.

apps.name: Meta Quest Link
apps.alternative: ALVR or WiVRn (wireless PC VR for Quest)
apps.why: Meta's Link software is Windows-only.

apps.name: Anti-cheat services
apps.why: Anti-cheat is installed per game. Games whose anti-cheat supports Proton work; kernel-level ones (Vanguard) don't.

apps.name: NVIDIA CUDA toolkit
apps.why: HalOS installs CUDA with the NVIDIA driver when an NVIDIA GPU is found (package cuda); the Windows components aren't moved.

apps.name: BakkesMod
apps.why: BakkesMod injects into the Windows Rocket League client; under Proton it needs manual setup and often breaks.

apps.name: NVIDIA software
apps.why: HalOS installs the NVIDIA driver itself; recording is done with OBS or GPU Screen Recorder.

apps.name: Wacom Tablet
apps.why: Wacom tablets work without a driver on HalOS (Settings > Drawing Tablet).

apps.name: Windows antivirus
apps.why: Windows antivirus isn't needed on HalOS; ClamAV is in the Store if you want a scanner.

apps.name: Uninstallers and driver updaters
apps.why: The Store removes apps cleanly; drivers come with system updates.

apps.name: Microsoft Edge WebView2
apps.why: A Windows component; nothing to bring.

apps.name: Windows runtimes
apps.why: Windows runtimes and components. Wine and Proton bring their own; nothing to move.

apps.name: Hardware drivers
apps.why: Hardware support is in the Linux kernel on HalOS; vendor driver packs aren't used.
